given.note: S13-32 and A3-12 with no turn: as j3-stop-tells-businesses.json, except that PostgreSQL was down when Alex texted only STOP at 12:45pm, so his handle actor sent the stop reply straight through Linq from its local copy and writes the record on return (caller.kind actorOnReturn, turnId null, as start-recorded.json does for Ben's START; arch 11 line 566; README default 6). The record has no turn, so its commit cannot write an outbox row (K-04 outbox_rows.turn_id is not null). For Lee's Barbershop, which has Alex's open booking (booking-alex-sam-book, booked), it writes instead one K-04 clock_rows row of kind step (fires: S13-32's notice, the fixed line textsOffReachTheirWay), owned by Sam's handle, with the barbershop's business id and that booking, armed and due at once in the business's zone; its firing, a clock turn on Sam's handle (its one event id the clock row's id: README default 24), writes the notice row to Sam within the minute (Sam's actor at once, else the minute sweep: arch 10 line 540), held for his text hours as any owner row is, never saying where the stop came from, and nothing is texted to Alex (README default 56; open gap 43). So businessesTold names the barbershop with no row yet. A page's or an email's STOP for the caller's own number (caller.kind page, inboundEventId null) tells each business the same way. The visit stays booked: alone, a stop never cancels it (S13-32). phoneVersion 5 is an example.
